ground.note: `--background` is `color-mix(in srgb, var(--primary) 7%, #F6F6F9)`: the page ground carries the user's accent at 7%, so it changes with the accent and is never a second hue. Dark: #0E1014.

card.note: `--card` / `--popover`: the white surface every piece of content sits on (the `panel` utility). Dark: card #171A21, popover #1B1F27.

muted-text.note: 30 Sep 2026: darkened from #6B7280 so it holds 4.9:1 on the darkest tinted ground (ink accent at 7%) and every soft fill. Dark: #9AA0AB.

brand-red.note: Logo slash, raven eye, tagline second line, eyebrow numbers, live dot. Brand surfaces only; never UI.

brand-ink.note: Brand panel, mark tile, email band.

brand-red-text-on-ink.note: Small red text on brand ink, 5.2:1.

accent-fill.note: Default of nine pastel accents (9 Oct 2026): red, blue, indigo, violet, teal, green, sky, plum, ink. Each sets --primary (fill), --primary-foreground (deep text on fill), --primary-text, --accent, --accent-foreground and --ring.

display.purpose: Sign-in, reset and email-link h1 (Chakra Petch 600, 24 px).

title.purpose: Page and pane titles in Chakra Petch, 17 px — the one brand mark inside the app besides the logo and the numbered panel labels.

figure-hero.purpose: 24 px (six sizes, 9 Oct 2026), Inter 600, leading-none, tracking-tight: the hero numbers (progress, tasks completed, Time on Odin; 17 px on a phone).

figure-tile.purpose: 24 px, Inter 600, leading-none: a tile's headline count.

figure-donut.purpose: 17 px, Inter 600: the total inside a donut.

figure-tonal.purpose: 17 px, Inter 600: the small tonal tiles (cycle time).

figure-legend.purpose: 14 px, Inter 500, tabular: a legend's counts.

body.purpose: Nav pills (500), rail copy, empty states, inputs, table cells. 13 px.

body-strong.purpose: Rollout name in a list row (14 px / 500); dashboard widget titles and the calendar month (14 px / 600).

secondary.purpose: Subtitles, stage node names (600), tasks, filter chips, notes, success notice. 13 px.

label.purpose: State chips (500), rail / panel section headers and My work group heads (600, chrome text), policy help. Sentence case, never tracked caps. 12 px.

caption.purpose: Column heads, durations and SLA under node names, settings group labels, calendar day chips, pop-up table heads. 12 px.

micro.purpose: Time-strip ticks, chart axis ticks, count badges, avatar initials (22–24 px avatars), due dates under tasks, figure labels. 11 px: the floor. The only sizes under it are the 10 px initials in a 20 px task avatar and the bell's 10 px unread pill, both glyph-sized, and the 10.5 px brand byline.

brand-display-sm.purpose: Tagline on the sign-in panel below 640 px (22 px).

brand-display-md.purpose: Tagline on the sign-in panel from 640 px (28 px).

brand-display.purpose: Tagline on the sign-in panel from 1024 px and the link preview (52 px).

byline.purpose: "by Protect24x7" beside the wordmark on brand surfaces (Chakra Petch 10.5 px, tracked 0.16em, uppercase).

shadows.name: elevation-card
shadows.purpose: Every card at rest (`panel`), the nav pill bar, the search pill, the dashboard customise bar, the lifted segment of a segmented control. In dark the first layer is a 1 px white-at-3% ring because a drop shadow alone vanishes on ink.

shadows.name: elevation-pop
shadows.purpose: Floating surfaces: the phone nav sheet, chart tooltips, menus and dialogs. Never on a card at rest.

focusRings.name: ring-focus
focusRings.purpose: focus-visible on buttons, inputs, scroll viewports; border switches to --ring.

focusRings.name: ring-state
focusRings.purpose: Current stepper dot and current stage node; --muted when on track. Also the ring around a stuck rollout bar on the calendar (state-line).

focusRings.name: ring-selected
focusRings.purpose: Selected rollout row; active command-palette row and current settings menu item take the wash alone.

motion.name: transition-colors
motion.purpose: Hover/selection on rows, chips, nav pills, buttons (Tailwind default).

motion.name: reduce-motion
motion.purpose: Every transition and animation is effectively off under the OS setting; Recharts animations are off unconditionally.

on_track.note: No chip, no row dot; current dot/node ringed ink over --muted. On the calendar and timeline an on-track rollout bar is the accent, not green.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "Cards on a tinted ground" (29 Sep 2026, the user's call, from a TaskFlux reference)**

Odin answers one question before anything is read: where is every rollout, and what is stuck. The built world is the soft card dashboard: a ground faintly tinted with the user's accent (`color-mix(in srgb, var(--primary) 7%, #F6F6F9)`), white cards with 16 px corners lifted by a quiet two-layer shadow, pill navigation with the current tab filled in the accent, and inside the cards the same ink text, hairlines and drawn flowchart as before. There is exactly one accent per user (eight to choose from), spent on selection, the primary action, focus, the current nav pill and the "today" marker. Every other colour on the screen is a state (done, on track, due soon / over SLA, overdue) and means nothing else. This replaces the 8 Sep "whiteboard flowchart" world (white ground, no shadows, 8 px corners); what follows records the build.

Density is high but scannable. The first screen is a resizable vertical split: a list of rollout rows above (stuck rows first, each carrying a 7-dot stepper), and the selected rollout below drawn as a left-to-right flowchart with its open tasks hung under the current node, a right rail for next-up / ETA / advance, a time strip along the bottom, and the team and recent notes under it (after the rail below `xl`). Type is small (13 px body) but never below 11 px, and nothing is uppercased. Every piece of content sits on a card (`panel`): the two flow panes, each settings section, every table, tile and widget.

The build rejected, by the user's explicit choice, the dark/industrial look, kanban-style SaaS boards and number-dense grids. Where the direction contract and the build differ, this file records the build.
keyCharacteristics: Accent-tinted ground, white cards, ink text, one accent per user; state colours in matched text / soft-fill / line triplets
Inter for everything read or typed, with `cv11` + `ss01`; Chakra Petch for page titles and brand surfaces only; sentence case in the UI, tracked caps only on brand surfaces
16 px base radius (`--radius: 1rem`) scaled by shadcn's ratios; pills and dots are fully round
Hairline 1 px borders (`#E9EAF0`); 1.5 px strokes only for flow geometry (nodes, dots, connectors)
Two shadow tokens, `shadow-card` (cards at rest) and `shadow-pop` (menus, the phone nav); focus and selection are 3 px translucent rings
Master-detail vertical split; flowchart nodes with drawn arrows at `md` and up, stacked without arrows below

rules.name: The Red-Text Rule
rules.body: The parent red (`#E11D2E`) is 4.2:1 on brand ink: fine for the logo, the eye, the dot and the 30 px+ tagline, not for small text. Small red text (eyebrow numbers, the byline's "24x7") uses `--brand-red-text`, which is the parent red on white (4.75:1) and lifts to `#F23D4D` inside `.brand-panel` (5.2:1).

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: The accent appears only as selection (row border + wash, the current nav pill), the primary action, the focus ring and chart marks. It never labels a state, never decorates, never appears as a heading colour, and never marks today (today is ink, so a red accent never reads as overdue).

rules.name: The Colour-Is-State Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red mean done / warning / overdue and nothing else. `on_track` has *no* colour: an on-track row shows a plain grey duration and a transparent dot, so a coloured row is always a row needing attention.

rules.name: The Triplet Rule
rules.body: State text uses the base token, state fills use `-soft`, state strokes and dots use `-line`. Never put the text shade in a fill or the line shade under text.

rules.name: The Accent-as-Text Rule
rules.body: When the accent is text or a thin mark on white, use `--primary-text` (`#B4143C` for red), not `--primary`; the pastel fill carries only `--primary-foreground`.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: No uppercase, no letter-spaced labels in the UI. A label is 12 px, weight 600, chrome text. Tracked caps belong to the brand surfaces only (panel, byline, eyebrows, print header, email).

rules.name: The Six-Size Rule
rules.body: The app uses six sizes: 11 (micro), 12 (captions, labels, chips), 13 (body), 14 (names, buttons), 17 (page and pane titles) and 24 (display titles and figures). Nothing in the app goes above 24 px or below 11 px; the half-pixel steps are gone. Hierarchy beyond that is carried by weight and by grey level (muted text), never by another size. Brand surfaces keep their own sizes (the 52 px tagline, the 10.5 px byline), and phone inputs stay 16 px so iOS does not zoom.

rules.name: The Stuck-First Rule
rules.body: The list is ordered by state severity, and on load it opens at the top; the deep-linked row is scrolled into view only after a click so the stuck rows are never hidden.

rules.name: The Card Rule
rules.body: Content sits on a `panel`, and a panel never sits inside another one (it becomes a tone step). Never hand-roll `border border-border rounded-lg`; use `panel` or a tone. Never invent a shadow value; the two tokens are the scale.

rules.name: The Grid Rule
rules.body: Every padding, margin and gap is a multiple of 4 px (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32…): no 2, 6, 10 or 14 px steps (`*-0.5`, `*-1.5`, `*-2.5`, `*-3.5`) in spacing. Icon sizes are not spacing and keep their steps.

rules.name: The Same-Column Rule
rules.body: Every row places its dots on one shared column order (the union of all rows' stage lists, each list keeping its own order), so a stage sits in the same column on every row and the lead can read down a column; a stage a project doesn't have leaves a gap on its line. Above the list, on every width, a scrolling strip of named stage pills ("PO Received 13") counts the rollouts in each stage under the current filter; a pill filters the list to that stage (lit ink with ×, kept in the URL). Pills and filter chips are 32 px, 40 px under a coarse pointer; a filter that would change nothing ("Mine" when you are on every rollout) is not offered. Done: `ok-line` fill and border, green connector. Current: white dot, state-line border, 3 px state-soft ring (ink border + Muted Fill ring when on track); scales to 110% when the row is selected. Upcoming: Stroke-grey border, white fill, grey connector. Each dot is a tooltip trigger ("Scoping · done"); the whole stepper carries an `aria-label` naming the current stage.

rules.name: The State-Safe Accent Rule
rules.body: An accent whose text or wash could pass for a state keeps its hue only in the pastel fill; red and green fall back to ink for text, wash and ring. Blue is the default.

dos: **Do** keep the accent to selection, the single primary action, focus and chart marks; today is ink (The One Accent Rule).
**Do** map rollout state to its triplet exactly: `overdue` → `bad`, `due_soon` and `over_sla` → `warn`, done stages → `ok`; `on_track` gets no colour.
**Do** pair every state colour with a second channel — the chip text, a visually-hidden label, the check glyph, dashed vs solid borders.
**Do** use `--primary-text` for accent-coloured text on white.
**Do** build on the base-nova components with the `render` prop; apply `buttonVariants()` to anchors that navigate to un-ported Jinja pages.
**Do** keep chrome at 12–13 px, sentence case, weight 500–600, in Chrome Text or Muted Text.
**Do** use 1 px hairlines for structure and 1.5 px strokes only for flow geometry (nodes, dots, connectors, today marker).
**Do** put every piece of content on a `panel`; convey depth inside a card with fill steps (Card → Muted Fill → Accent Wash).
donts: **Don't** add a third shadow value or a gradient; the ground tint is the accent at 7% and never a second hue.

**Don't** uppercase or letter-space UI labels, or bring back the retired dark nav, 2 px corners, or the 8 Sep flat white ground. Brand red and Chakra Petch are allowed only where "Brand surfaces" lists them; red never marks anything in the UI except `--bad` state.
**Don't** use green for "on track" rows or amber/red for anything that is not a lateness state; don't use `--destructive` for rollout state.
**Don't** put a state's text shade in a fill or its line shade under text.

**Don't** invent tokens: use the `:root` block in `frontend/src/index.css` and its `@theme inline` aliases (`ok-*`, `warn-*`, `bad-*`, `primary-text`, `nav-fg`). Dark and the accents are whole-token overrides (`:root[data-theme="dark"]`, `:root[data-accent=…]`); a component never branches on the theme.
**Don't** render the flow as a kanban board or a numeric table; the stepper and the node row are the read.
